pairing.directionPolicy: Each canonical pair owns two separately reviewed directional invocations.
pairing.selfTransitionPolicy: Repeated letters are reinforcement transitions outside the 231-Gate registry.

defaultRule.reason: No Gate becomes executable until its directional rule and technical basis are explicitly reviewed.

rules.technicalBasis: Reference rule for the canonical אור acceptance program: Aleph frame followed by Vav exchange.

directions.description: The preserved frame hands its trace to the Vav exchange across shared machine state.
The reverse invocation remains reserved for separate review.

rules.technicalBasis: Reference rule for the canonical אור acceptance program: Vav exchange followed by Resh reseed.

directions.description: The Vav exchange arrives at Yesod and continues through the Resh reseed toward Malchut.
The reverse invocation remains reserved for separate review.

scientificBoundary: Gate rules are deterministic software contracts inspired by the traditional 231 letter pairs. They are not evidence of physical quantum behavior or inherent natural operations in Hebrew letters.
